subject: Re: Significant p99 spikes on long-context (8k/16k/32k) - MedSync
messages:
From: Cara Lopez <cara@medsync.ai>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-12-09T08:14:22-08:00
Subject: Spike in p99 latency for large patient notes (32k)

Jonas / Redwood team,

We started seeing a big jump in p99 latency and intermittent 500 errors on our production integration around 07:50 PST this morning. The effect is concentrated on requests with long context (we're pushing full patient notes up to 32k tokens for summarization).

Symptoms:
- p50/p90 are generally fine but p99 has jumped from ~800ms to 6–8s for 32k windows.
- Small-context calls (<=8k) are unaffected.
- Error rate on the hosted API rose to ~2.3% for our tenant for about 20 minutes.

We've attached a short sample payloads file and some timestamps (ops@medsync.ai copied). Can you triage urgently? Our care routing depends on this.

Thanks,
Cara Lopez
CTO, MedSync Health
cara@medsync.ai

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: Cara Lopez <cara@medsync.ai>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-12-09T08:22:11-08:00
Subject: Re: Spike in p99 latency for large patient notes (32k)

Cara — thanks for the alert and the sample payloads. We're pulling the initial telemetry now.

Quick plan (30m window):
1) Engineering will check serving pools for MedSync tenant (soojin & karthik).
2) We'll test a conservative tenant-level throttle for requests > 16k tokens to prevent queue build-up.
3) If recent kernel changes correlate with this window we'll roll back the change for the affected pool.

Can you join a 30-min call at 08:45 PST? If not, we'll proceed with mitigation and keep you updated.

Jonas Weber
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.ai

From: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-12-09T08:30:05-08:00
Subject: Re: Spike in p99 latency for large patient notes (32k) — initial triage

On Wed, Dec 9, 2026 at 08:22 AM jonas_weber@redwood.ai wrote:
> Cara — thanks for the alert and the sample payloads. We're pulling the initial telemetry now.

Initial findings from the serving telemetry (preliminary):
- Host pool RB-14 shows sustained request queueing beginning 07:48 PST. CPU/GPU utilization is high; rare OOMs not correlated with error spikes.
- KV cache churn increases substantially for requests >16k tokens (32k particularly). Cache miss/eviction rate is 4–5x baseline for MedSync traffic.
- The new multi-threaded attention kernel rolled out to RB-14 yesterday shows a spike in tail latency when context >24k under small batch sizes; likely scheduling contention.

Immediate mitigations in priority order:
- Apply tenant-level soft throttle for requests >16k (max concurrent long-context = 3).
- Temporarily reduce max_batch_size on RB-14 for MedSync to avoid cross-tenant contention.
- Roll back the attention kernel on RB-14 if mitigations don't reduce p99 within 10–15m.

I've attached the raw extraction (initial-triage.txt) and included correlating traces. We'll re-evaluate within 15 minutes and update Cara directly.

— Soojin
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.ai

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: Cara Lopez <cara@medsync.ai>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-12-09T08:40:33-08:00
Subject: Re: Spike in p99 latency for large patient notes (32k) — mitigation plan and call

Cara — quick update: Engineering applied a soft tenant throttle and reduced batch sizes for your tenant on the affected pool at 08:35 PST. We're seeing p99 reduce from ~6s down to ~1.2–1.8s for the 32k samples in our tests; error rate trending down.

We still recommend a short diagnostics call so we can confirm end-to-end for your production traffic and agree on a longer-term fix (kernel rollback vs. targeted kernel patch). Are you available now for a 20-min check-in?

Temporary mitigations noted:
- tenant.long_context_concurrency = 3
- max_batch_size override = 8 for RB-14

We expect full stability or a clear rollback decision within 30m.

Thanks,
Jonas

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-12-09T11:02:05-08:00
Subject: Exec summary: MedSync p99 surge (post-mitigation)

Team — closing notes from the morning escalation (summary for leadership):
- Timeline: spike began ~07:48 PST, mitigations applied 08:35 PST, persistent regression mitigated by tenant throttle and batch-size override by ~08:40 PST.
- Root cause (prelim): interaction between the recently deployed multi-threaded attention kernel and long-context scheduling on RB-14 under MedSync's workload (32k windows). Kernel triggers excessive KV churn and scheduling stalls at tail.
- Customer impact: elevated p99 (6–8s) and transient error rate (~2.3%) for ~20 minutes. MedSync requests are business-critical (care routing).
- Customer ask: credit for the incident window and committed follow-up: full rollback or targeted kernel patch plus improved tenant isolation controls.

Requested next steps / approvals:
1) Approve one-time credit proposal (Neha: customer is asking for a commercial remedy; see attached proposed-credit.pdf).
2) Engineering to schedule kernel rollback or patch release ASAP; Soojin to own the rollback.
3) Postmortem and longer-term fixes (postmortem-plan.md) — schedule within 72 hours and share with MedSync.

I'll coordinate timelines and the customer comms.

Jonas Weber
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.ai
